decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Depth Severances and Formation Rights in Mineral Valuation
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 61ce051f7f3f5e475dd9a2d1f39697db83d28fd99f23b1636a9963581464d807; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.
Deed-construction, subsurface-property, recording, regulatory-field, well-log, completion, and property-appraisal claims remain bounded to their official court and government sources.

The article uses no fabricated instruments, legal descriptions, depth cutoffs, formations, owners, wells, production, leases, prices, reserves, percentages, disputes, transaction values, testimonials, or owner-specific legal or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Supreme Court of Texas, Wenske v. Ealy, No. 16-0353 (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Supreme Court of Texas explains that an unambiguous deed is construed from the intent expressed within the instrument as a whole, with provisions harmonized where possible.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the opinion only for the general deed-construction boundary and does not interpret a private instrument, resolve ambiguity, determine title, or apply the holding to an owner-specific dispute.

sources_inspected.label: Supreme Court of Texas, Myers-Woodward, LLC v. Underground Services Markham, LLC, No. 22-0878 (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Supreme Court of Texas distinguishes a conveyed mineral estate and associated production rights from underground empty space and evaluates the deed language and legal character of the claimed property interest.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the opinion as a limited illustration that subsurface property categories must be identified precisely; it does not extend the salt-cavern holding to a different mineral deed or depth boundary.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Legislature, Property Code (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Property Code provides the statutory recording framework for instruments concerning real property, including execution and acknowledgment requirements addressed by the cited provisions.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the Code only as recording context and does not claim that recording alone resolves title, instrument interpretation, notice disputes, or the validity of an owner-specific conveyance.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Glossary (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission glossary distinguishes fields, reservoirs, completion depth, and total depth, and explains that a field can contain separate reservoirs at different depths.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses these definitions to prevent regulatory and geological terms from being collapsed together; it does not treat a field assignment or reported depth as ownership evidence.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Glossary for Well Log List (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission well-log glossary identifies top and bottom log intervals, field, lease, API, survey, and total-depth data used to locate and understand Commission records.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the glossary for data-field boundaries and does not claim that a log interval, well identifier, or survey reference establishes private title or a legal depth cutoff.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, About Oil and Gas Data Queries (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission explains that a wellbore is the hole in the ground and can contain one or more completions, and that its query systems expose different regulatory data slices.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses this distinction for careful identity and completion matching and does not infer title, lease continuation, or payment ownership from the wellbore record.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller, Valuing Property (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller describes the sales-comparison, income, and cost approaches and explains that the income approach estimates the present worth of anticipated future benefits.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article preserves the public property-tax context and does not present the page as a private-sale formula, professional appraisal, title conclusion, or owner-specific value.
